Package de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.ui.skill

Class SkillCategoriesView

java.lang.Object
com.vaadin.flow.component.Component
com.vaadin.flow.component.splitlayout.SplitLayout
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.ui.skill.SkillCategoriesView
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.vaadin.flow.component.AttachNotifier, com.vaadin.flow.component.ClickNotifier<com.vaadin.flow.component.splitlayout.SplitLayout>, com.vaadin.flow.component.DetachNotifier, com.vaadin.flow.component.HasElement, com.vaadin.flow.component.HasSize, com.vaadin.flow.component.HasStyle, com.vaadin.flow.component.HasTheme, com.vaadin.flow.component.shared.HasThemeVariant<com.vaadin.flow.component.splitlayout.SplitLayoutVariant>, Serializable
@Route("skill-categories") @PermitAll public class SkillCategoriesView extends com.vaadin.flow.component.splitlayout.SplitLayout
Master-detail admin CRUD screen for the SkillCategory tree that the SkillsView categories hang off: name, description and an optional parent category. Admin-only (behind the login), so — like the underlying SkillService category methods and the sibling RoleView — it carries no PUser/permission check.

Rows and the parent selector are SkillCategoryDTO, never the entity: SkillCategory's all-fields equals/hashCode touches its lazy parentCategory/subCategories and would throw a LazyInitializationException inside a Vaadin grid/ComboBox (see GroupsView). The parent selector excludes the category being edited (blocks trivial self-parenting); deleting a category removes its whole subtree and detaches affected skills — SkillService#deleteCategory does this via a recursive query, and the notification says so.

Author:
peter haller
